hook.line: English puts my in front of everything: my hands, my hair, my house. Spanish only does it for some of those. Here's how to tell which.
hook.es: Me lavo las manos y me voy a mi casa.
hook.en: I wash my hands and go home.

examples.en: I try your jacket on. (to a friend)

rule:
Your body, and the clothes you have on, already belong to you. Spanish doesn't bother saying so with *mi* or *mis*; the little word *me*, *te* or *se*, or simply who the sentence is about, does that job. The body part gets *el*, *la*, *los* or *las*:

*Me lavo las manos.* I wash my hands.
*Tomás cierra los ojos.* Tomás closes his eyes.
*Vale tiene el pelo largo.* Vale has long hair.

Everything else, the things you own but aren't part of you, keeps *mi*, *tu*, *su*: *mi casa*, *mi café*, *tu celular*.

When it's someone else's body, the little word changes instead: *Te lavo el pelo* is I wash your hair. When it's someone else's jacket, say whose: *Me pruebo tu chaqueta* is I try your jacket on.
smallPrint: With body parts and clothing, Spanish uses the definite article where English uses a possessive; the pronoun (or the subject) marks the owner.

options: Did you wash your face? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Vale se lava el pelo con mi champú.
options: Vale washes her hair with my shampoo.
Vale washes my hair with her shampoo.
I wash my hair with Vale's shampoo.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap with *el* or *mi*, then type the whole sentence: "*Me lavo ___ pelo.*"
yourTurn.why: *Me* already says it's your hair, so just *el*.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap with *la* or *mi*, then type the whole sentence: "*___ casa es grande.*" (My house is big.)
yourTurn.why: A house isn't part of you, and nothing else says whose, so keep *mi*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Tomás closes his eyes.
yourTurn.why: They're Tomás's own eyes, so *los ojos* is enough.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale has long hair.
yourTurn.why: Spanish says she has the hair long: *el pelo*, not *su pelo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: My café is small.
yourTurn.why: A café belongs to you but isn't part of you: *mi*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: "*Me lavo la cara.*"
yourTurn.why: *Nos* says whose faces; each of us has one, so it stays *la cara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make the jacket a friend's: "*Me pruebo la chaqueta.*" Say: I try your jacket on.
yourTurn.why: When it's someone else's, Spanish says so with *tu*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Me* already says they're your hands; *mis* says it twice.
His own eyes need no *sus*; *Tomás* already says whose.

personal: Describe yourself in one line with *tengo* and a body part (*Tengo el pelo...*), then one line about something you own with *mi*.
